title.narrative: Output 3.2. Increased capacity of member States to formulate and implement policies and strategies for creating decent work in the rural economy

description.narrative:
Local government authorities and institutions in three regions of Moldova have operationalised measures for decent work in rural areas through local employment partnerships (LEPs). LEPs have been designed and implemented as stand-alone initiatives for job creation and transition to formality in rural areas. They have also supported the decentralised implementation of the national employment strategy of Moldova (2017-2021). LEP interventions focussed in particular on creating employment opportunities for women in rural areas and reaching out and activating young people, who represent a large share of the potential labour force and are important agents of change towards a human-centred rural transformation in Moldova. With RBSA resources, the ILO worked with the local government authorities and the local branches of the social partners in three rural regions (Cahul, Cantemir, Causeni) to jointly identify context-specific solutions to local labour market challenges. The ILO’s technical assistance included support to territorial audits, capacity building of the local tripartite councils, adaptation of ILO training tools for entrepreneurship, handicraft, cooperatives, and value chain development, access to finance (in partnership with the Organization for Small and Medium Enterprise Sector Development, ODIMM, and local providers of private sector financing, such as the Savings and Credit Association), as well as support to local and national institutions to monitor results and identify opportunities for scaling-up and replication.
With the support of the Government of Austria to a joint UN programme, the ILO provided support to the LEPs in Causeni and Cantemir focused on the provision of job opportunities to women in rural areas who had to return from migration due to the Covid-19 pandemic and on building institutional capacities of the national employment agency (NEA) to deal with the specific employment challenges of women returnees.

Output 5.2. Increased capacity of member States to strengthen skills and lifelong learning policies, governance models and financing system

description.narrative:
Six sector skills committees were successfully established and formally registered in the following sectors: Light Industry, Agriculture, HoReCa (Hotels, Restauration, Catering), Construction, ITC and Water Distribution/Sanitation (including waste/decontamination).
53 members of industry associations and government institutions (Ministry of Labour, Ministry of Education) benefitted directly from the information sources developed and the training activities (workshops, e-learning, access to information) organised by the project in the following areas: - Establishment and legal registration of a Sector Skills Committee. - Project development and implementation. - Skills needs anticipation at sectoral level / STED. - Development of occupational standards.
The Sector Skills Committees developed skills related projects, the most prominent among them being: - The establishment of working groups for the development of occupational standards for occupations in agriculture, commerce and tourism and light industry. Each working group includes 20 sector experts (60 persons in total) who improved their capacities in the development of occupational standards. - The organization of the competition "Best In the Job" with CoEs of companies and TVET schools in two sectors: light industry and waste management. The project included around 30 persons per sector (60 persons in total). - The exchange of experience with Romanian sectoral associations in the construction sector, thereby strengthening the skills of 30 beneficiaries. - A communication workshop for increasing networking among stakeholders in the three sectors: commerce, tourism and agriculture. About 40 persons per sector benefitted from this activity (120 beneficiaries in total). With RBSA resources, the ILO advised representatives of Social Partners and line ministries in setting-up and legally registering six Sector Skills Committees.
The ILO designed and implemented tailor-made capacity-building workshops and established an e-learning and information platform to provide guidance and equip members of industry associations and line ministries with knowledge and skills in the following areas: - Establishment and legal registration of a Sector Skills Committee. - Project development and implementation. - Skills needs anticipation at sectoral level / STED - Development of occupational standards.
Furthermore, the ILO supported the Sector Skills Committees in the development of the above-mentioned project proposals.
